existing_incident_edges_inspected.relationship: Nora’s lieux de mémoire distinguish lived social memory from historical reconstruction and examine their materialized sites.
existing_incident_edges_inspected.evidence_note: Own 1989 pp7–9; the opposition is his argument, not a universal analytical law.

existing_incident_edges_inspected.relationship: Nora historicizes the national framework of French memory and its weakening, connecting historiographical practice to changing collective identifications.
existing_incident_edges_inspected.evidence_note: Own 1989 pp10–12 discussion of nation, memory and historiography; selected French case, not a general claim about national histories.

existing_incident_edges_inspected.relationship: Nora expressly invokes Halbwachs’s account of group-specific, plural memories while distinguishing memory from historical reconstruction (1989 English translation).
existing_incident_edges_inspected.evidence_note: Printed p. 9, first paragraph, read in Marc Roudebush’s translation, alongside pp. 7–8. Nora’s memory/history opposition and civilizational language remain his historically situated formulation; the original French and Halbwachs’s full works are not newly collated.

existing_incident_edges_inspected.relationship: Nora’s invitation to introduce O’Connell’s collection brought Le Goff to Saint Louis’s reported words, an encounter he identifies in explaining the origin of his biographical project.
existing_incident_edges_inspected.evidence_note: Le Goff’s own opening account credits an editorial invitation and the resulting source encounter. O’Connell compiled the texts; Nora did not write them or supply the whole biography’s method. The retrospective approximate project date is not a precisely dated commission.

existing_incident_edges_inspected.relationship: Charle credits the merits of the Lieux de mémoire project but argues that its popularity returned historians to cultural and national frames.
existing_incident_edges_inspected.evidence_note: Own December 2007 answer, published 2008, 163–164, explicitly says that he participated without following the master-builder’s intended direction. The institutional bibliography identifies Pierre Nora as editor of the specific 1986 and 1992 Lieux volumes to which Charle contributed; the interview’s unnamed editor is identified through that metadata, not presented as an explicit spoken naming. This is a qualified objection to a project’s framing and reception, not a rejection of memory research or adjudication of every chapter. Original volumes unread.

existing_incident_edges_inspected.relationship: Uses Nora’s lieux de mémoire to treat changing traces and appropriations of the past as objects of historical inquiry.
existing_incident_edges_inspected.evidence_note: Own 2011 discussion identifies a methodological opening across periods, reinforced in 2012 and 2017 conclusion. This is specific analytical use, not a resource inferred merely because Dosse wrote Nora’s biography. The complete original collective work unread. Own 2012 additionally recalls Nora supplying crucial details during biographical research under an agreement to maintain distance; this bounded informant contribution is consolidated here, not a claim Nora controlled or endorsed the finished book.

existing_incident_edges_inspected.relationship: Winter credits Nora’s sites-of-memory project with expanding his evidentiary resources while developing an international, comparative study of mourning.
existing_incident_edges_inspected.evidence_note: Own 1995 book introduction 10 explicitly says gained much from extraordinary project and praises brilliant contributions/evidentiary expansion, immediately specifying different objectives. 1999 joint 37/n54 uses Nora 1989 for material memory aids. Particular resource coexists with criticism of national framing and premature obituary of living memory; not influence inferred from similar titles, whole collective assigned to Nora alone or original Nora reading claimed.

existing_incident_edges_inspected.relationship: Winter challenges Nora’s national framing and, with Sivan, his claim that living collective memory, ritual and literature have disappeared.
existing_incident_edges_inspected.evidence_note: Own 1995 introduction 10 criticizes French-only, antiquarian/reverential framing and lack of systematic comparison while praising project. Joint 1999 introduction 1–3 calls obituary premature, cites living ritual/family narratives/novels and questions generalization beyond France. Joint authorship retained; cited Nora Realms of Memory 1996 trans Arthur Goldhammer distinguished from 1989 article and collective French volumes. Original Nora unread; not blanket denial of sites/material aids or claim all chapters identical.
